summary: Smith Mountain Lookout traces to a 1908 fire camp and stands today as a 1963 cab on a 10-foot concrete base, staffed intermittently since the 1930s.

facts.design: L-4 style, 16x16-foot cab on 10-foot concrete base

access.note: Drive-up access; current status is emergency use, not a public rental.

visit.trail_note: Reachable by drive-up road per Idaho Fire Lookouts.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Payette National Forest

events.note: A fire-watch camp was established on Smith Mountain.
A cupola-style cabin was built to house the lookout.
The cupola cabin was replaced by an L-4 cab.
Current lookout built: 16x16-foot cab on a 10-foot concrete base.
Mr. and Mrs. Hubert Fuller staffed the lookout, 1947-1949.
Wiggins staffed the lookout again, per Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register on September 29, 2020.

evidence.quote: Established with a camp in 1908, a cupola cabin was built in 1920.
This was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1932.
The present 10' concrete base with 16x16' cab, built in 1963, is available for emergencies.
Known lookout personnel: 1939: Emerson Wiggins; 1942: Clarke Childers; 1947-1949: Mr. & Mrs. Hubert Fuller.
2020 – Added to the National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict in brief (1963 per NHLR vs. longer history) resolves cleanly: 1908 camp, 1920 cupola cabin, 1932 L-4, 1963 current structure, per FireLookout.com detail not captured by the brief's single NHLR 'Built' field.
